snapshots.title: Fix UAF in io_uring submit: handle EAGAIN like EBUSY
snapshots.body:
Fixes #8255

When the kernel returns EAGAIN from io_uring_enter, the SQE is already queued in the submission ring. submit() returned the error, and register_op's submit_or_remove closure called remove_op() + Op::poll dropped the data the SQE points to. A later successful submit executing the stale SQE against freed memory causes use-after-free.
snapshots.author: VrtxOmega

snapshots.title: fix(io_uring): prevent use-after-free on failed submit
snapshots.body:
Fixes #8255

This PR implements maintainer's proposed solution:

1). Treat EAGAIN like EBUSY in the submit loop to drain completions and retry.

2). If submit fails after an SQE is queued, leave the operation in the slab.

3). register_op now returns the index on failure. Op::poll uses this to upgrade its state to Polled and returns Pending. When the future drops, the memory is safely moved to Lifecycle::Cancelled until the kernel's CQE arrives.

snapshots.title: runtime: keep io_uring op alive when submission fails after push
snapshots.body:
## Motivation

In the io_uring backend, `register_op` pushes an SQE onto the submission queue
and then calls `submit()`. If `submit()` returns any error other than `EBUSY`,
the op is removed from the slab, which drops the operation and frees the buffer
the SQE points at.

This is unsound. `io_uring_enter` advances the submission queue head as it
consumes SQEs, so a non-`EBUSY` error does not mean the kernel never saw the
entry — it may have already accepted it. In that case the kernel can still write
into the buffer we just freed (use-after-free), and the eventual CQE refers to a
slab slot that no longer exists, which panics the driver or, if the slot has
been reused, completes an unrelated op.

## Solution

Once the SQE has been pushed, keep the slab entry even if `submit()` fails, the
same way the cancellation path does: the buffer stays alive until the completion
is observed, and the error is still propagated to the caller. The pre-push
submit (flushing a full queue) is unchanged, since there the entry has not
reached the kernel and removing it is correct.

Adds a regression test that forces a post-push submit failure and asserts the op
is retained. Verified on Linux 6.8 (io_uring enabled): the test fails before this
change and passes after, and the existing `fs_uring*` tests continue to pass.
snapshots.author: blasrodri

snapshots.title: mono: use resolved targets for method reachability
snapshots.body:
Fixes #258.

## Problem

Monomorphization handled an instance call such as `LoadError.message()` by enqueueing every method with the bare name `message`. That made unrelated stdlib methods reachable; the reporter reproduction then lowered `IoError_message` in the wrong program context and failed with `UnresolvedVariable("msg")`.

## Change

Pass the type checker TypedProgram into production monomorphization and use its CALL6 `Callee::Method` target as the exact reachable method. Keep the existing conservative bare-name fallback for standalone or unresolved cases that do not have a typed dispatch target.

## Verification

- Before: the release CLI failed on the issue reproduction with `MIR lowering 'IoError_message': UnresolvedVariable("msg")`.
- After: the same native run exits successfully and prints `1 2 3`, `none`, and `10 20 30`.
- `cargo test -p rask-mono` — 49 passed
- `cargo test -p rask-compiler` — 19 passed
- `cargo build --release -p rask-cli`
- `git diff --check`

## Risk

The production path now consumes the dispatch result already established by the type checker. The conservative fallback remains for callers without TypedProgram data.

## Assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex helped trace the failure, implement the patch, and run the checks. I reviewed the scoped diff and evidence before submission.

snapshots.title: Fix screenshot preview scrolling
snapshots.body:
Fixes #2817.

## Summary

- makes the screenshot preview pane vertically scrollable when a screenshot is taller than the preview viewport
- keeps horizontal overflow hidden so wide screenshots still fit the existing preview layout

## Before / After

- Before: long screenshots could be clipped inside the previewer with no scrollbar.
- After: the screenshot section owns its vertical overflow, so long screenshots can be scrolled without changing the other preview modes.

## Validation

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --ignore-path=.gitignore --check apps/web/components/dashboard/preview/LinkContentSection.tsx`
- `pnpm --filter @karakeep/web run lint`
- `pnpm --filter @karakeep/web run typecheck`
- `TZ=UTC pnpm --filter @karakeep/web run test -- --run`
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD`
- pre-commit hook: `turbo run --no-daemon typecheck lint format`
